inputs.source: On call engineer's chat request, authenticated via SSO

instructions.note: The agent will deploy any named service or run any named migration in production, with no allowlist, scoping, or restriction on which services or databases are valid targets.

The agent is explicitly instructed never to ask for confirmation before acting. This removes the only possible human-in-the-loop check prior to irreversible production actions; no other preventive safety mechanism is described anywhere in the design.
Framing the suppression of confirmation around the engineer 'being busy' implies every request should be treated as fully authorized and unambiguous, regardless of whether it actually is.

controls.name: Cloud audit log of production actions
controls.decay_rationale: Logging occurs outside the model and does not depend on model cooperation, so it does not decay with model capability. It is detective rather than preventive, so under rubric section 5 step 5 it earns no tier credit. It also records only the action and the engineer identity, not the request or rationale behind it.

controls.name: Human approval gate for production migrations
controls.decay_rationale: Not present in the design; the system prompt affirmatively instructs the agent to never ask for confirmation. If added with raw_action review showing the actual migration script and target database, it would not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Human approval gate for production deploys
controls.decay_rationale: Not present in the design for the same reason as the migration gate.

controls.name: Tamper-evident record of request intent linked to the audit log
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. The only current record of what was asked and why -- the chat transcript -- is deletable by the same engineer whose identity the cloud audit log uses to attribute the resulting production action, so no non-repudiation link exists between request and action.

findings.title: Unconfirmed, irreversible production database migration with no approval gate

attack_path.note: Engineer asks for a named migration to run in production.
Agent runs the migration immediately with the engineer's own credentials; the system prompt forbids asking for confirmation.

evidence.observation: Agent runs the named migration in production using the engineer's credentials whenever asked.
Agent is explicitly instructed not to ask for confirmation before acting.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically, making this sink irreversible.
No step limit, runtime limit, or approval gate of any kind is described for production actions.

recommendations.action: Require human approval, shown as the raw migration script and target database from the system of record, before any production migration runs.
Restrict migrations to a pre-reviewed allowlist rather than accepting any named migration.

findings.title: Unconfirmed production deploy with no approval gate

attack_path.note: Engineer asks for a named service to be deployed.
Agent deploys immediately with the engineer's own credentials; no confirmation is permitted.

evidence.observation: Agent deploys the named service in production using the engineer's credentials whenever asked.
Agent is explicitly instructed not to ask for confirmation before acting.
No step limit or runtime limit is declared, and the only control present (audit logging) is detective, not preventive.

recommendations.action: Add a confirmation step or restrict deploy targets to a pre-approved list of services, at least for the first deploy of a session.

findings.title: Non-repudiation gap: the sole record of request intent is deletable by the identity it attributes production actions to

attack_path.note: Engineer requests a production action via chat.
This request is recorded only in the chat transcript, which the requesting engineer can delete.
The action executes using the engineer's own token.
The audit log attributes the action to the engineer's name, but contains no record of what was asked or why.

evidence.observation: Every production action is recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name, using the engineer's own personal access token.
The only record of what the agent was asked, and why it acted, is the chat transcript, and engineers can delete their own chat history.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically, so the action this finding concerns is itself irreversible.

recommendations.action: Store the request transcript in a write-once store the requesting engineer cannot delete, correlated with the audit log entry by a shared request id, before the agent acts on it.
Alert or block when chat history underlying a logged production action is deleted before a defined retention period.

rating.rationale: The migration and deploy paths both run from a trusted, authenticated source to a significant or irreversible sink with no step or runtime limit, which triggers the autonomy modifier and raises the migration path to 'high' and the deploy path to 'moderate'. No preventive control exists for either path: the system prompt affirmatively forbids any confirmation step, and the only control present, the cloud audit log, is purely detective and earns no tier credit under rubric section 5. Residual therefore equals inherent for both. A third finding captures a related but distinct flaw: the sole record of what was requested and why, the chat transcript, is deletable by the same engineer whose identity the audit log uses to attribute the resulting production action, so the design cannot support non-repudiation or incident review for its most severe actions; this is also rated high with no credited mitigation. Because the gaps here are architectural omissions rather than controls that weaken as the model gets more capable, the forecast tier equals the residual tier (high); the one control present, the audit log, does not decay but also would not change the outcome if it were lost, so no single trigger moves this forecast further than the current design already allows.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.

No tool manifest, MCP config, or IaC was provided; the scope of which services or databases can be named is inferred from the system prompt rather than verified against an enumerated allowlist, so confidence on scope boundaries is medium.
The actual scope and lifetime of the engineer's personal access token, and the retention policy of the cloud audit log, are described only in prose and were not independently verified.
